tutorial.step1_text: Start by adding a high-level industrial process block for your facility using the 'Add Process' button.
tutorial.step2_text: Place your process geographically on the interactive map so you can visually plan piping and spatial constraints.
tutorial.step3_text: Break your process down into subprocesses and enter the thermodynamic stream data (Temperature and Mass Flow) for each component.
tutorial.step4_text: Review all the streams you've entered and select which ones you want to include in the potential analysis.
tutorial.step0_text:
Welcome to HeatTransPlan! This tool helps industrial facilities discover energy savings. Here is how the workflow is structured:

1) Data Collection & Facility Mapping
• Start by adding your main operational Processes.
• Break those down into specific Subprocesses (e.g., 'Cooling Tower', 'Boiler').
• For each subprocess, define the individual energy Streams (hot and cold). You must specify the Mass Flow, Heat Capacity (Cp), and the Input/Output Temperatures.
• Use the interactive Map to place your processes geographically, exactly where they are located in your real facility. This helps visualize spatial constraints for future pipe routing.

2) Potential Analysis & Heat Integration
• Review the Stream Summary table to ensure your thermodynamic data is correct.
• Select the specific streams you want to analyze.
• Run the Pinch Analysis to automatically generate Composite Curves. These graphs visually demonstrate your absolute maximum heat recovery potential and identify your 'Pinch Point'.
• Finally, explore Heat Pump Integration to bridge remaining temperature gaps using proposed real-world heat pump models (showing kW and COP parameters).

Click 'Next' to see a visual walkthrough of these steps!

status_quo.title: 📊 Comparison of Status Quo and Proposal
status_quo.desc: Compare the current external energy supply with the absolute minimum external energy required after maximal internal heat recovery (the proposal). Savings indicate how much external utility is avoided.
status_quo.warning: 💡 Current energy supplies are required to calculate the difference to status quo. Please configure them in the "Current energy supply" section above.

recovery.title: Heat recovery before integration
recovery.explanation_with: Net load curves — the pocket-free Grand Composite Curve split into a source and a sink profile. Heat is recovered wherever the temperatures allow it, so the heat pump only covers the utility demand that is left over. This is standard pinch practice and the recommended default.
recovery.explanation_no: Composite curves — hot and cold composite curves used directly as source and sink profiles. Internal heat recovery is not assumed, so the heat pump meets the full heating and cooling demands where possible.

stream_selector.title: Streams Selection
stream_selector.help_desc: Select which streams (heat sources or sinks) to include in the pinch analysis. Deselect streams that are currently inactive or should be excluded.

energy_demands.title: Current energy supply
energy_demands.help_desc: Define the baseline energy consumption (heating and cooling) for the selected streams. This represents the 'status quo' before heat integration.

optimization.tooltip_refrigerant_type: Classification of the refrigerant. Natural refrigerants (like Ammonia, CO2) have low environmental impact (GWP) but may have toxicity/flammability considerations. Synthetic refrigerants (like HFCs/HFOs) are traditionally used but often face strict regulations due to environmental impact.
optimization.tooltip_cop: Coefficient of Performance (COP): The ratio of useful heating or cooling provided to work (energy) required. Higher COP means greater efficiency.
optimization.tooltip_q_sink: Heat capacity delivered to the sink (the amount of heat the heat pump provides to the process).
optimization.tooltip_q_source: Heat capacity extracted from the source (the amount of heat the heat pump absorbs from the process or environment).
optimization.tooltip_temp_sink: The target temperature at which heat is delivered to the sink.
optimization.tooltip_temp_source: The temperature at which heat is extracted from the source.
optimization.tooltip_refrigerant: The specific chemical refrigerant used in the heat pump cycle.
optimization.tooltip_hp_stages: The number of compression stages used in the heat pump system. More stages can improve efficiency across large temperature lifts.

panel.title: Integration with Heat Pump model and optimization
panel.instruction: Click on any column header to sort. Click on any point in the chart to inspect its details and add it to the table.

filters.source_limited_desc: These cover only part of the demand above T_sink, so they lie off the sink profile.
filters.demand_limited_desc: These cover the full demand but leave waste heat unused at T_source, so they lie off the source profile.
filters.custom_cop_desc: Paste a custom COP to perform integration and optimization with your own heat pump.

optimization.desc_actual_source_temp: The physical evaporation temperature of the heat pump. (Note: In some specific pocket configurations, this physical temperature may align with the integration temperature).
optimization.desc_shifted_source_temp: The shifted temperature on the Grand Composite Curve (Actual - ΔTmin/2). This is the temperature used for the COP calculation.
optimization.desc_actual_sink_temp: The physical condensation temperature of the heat pump. (Note: In some specific pocket configurations, this physical temperature may align with the integration temperature).
optimization.desc_shifted_sink_temp: The shifted temperature on the Grand Composite Curve (Actual + ΔTmin/2). This is the temperature used for the COP calculation.
optimization.desc_model_information: Please note that the Heat Pump model provided by Copeland is based on physical simulations and yields approximations intended for reference purposes only. For precise calculations or project-specific data, please contact Copeland directly.
optimization.desc_medium_sink: The sink medium for this integration
optimization.desc_hp_simulates: Simulates the integration of various heat pump types to upgrade waste heat from below the pinch to satisfy demands above the pinch, further reducing external utility consumption.

optimization.desc_hpi_chart_p3: Heat pumps reduce both external heating and cooling demands simultaneously.

optimization.desc_gcc_chart_p2: Pockets in the curve (where it moves right then left) show where heat can be cascaded internally without external utilities.
optimization.desc_gcc_chart_p3: The top-right and bottom-right edges show the remaining external hot and cold utility targets.

optimization.desc_cc_chart_p3: The vertical distance between the curves represents the temperature difference driving the heat transfer.

optimization.desc_opt_chart_p2: Solid diamonds represent the source points, and open diamonds represent the sink points. Colors correspond to the refrigerant used.
optimization.desc_opt_chart_p3: The large highlighted points indicate the optimal solution or the one you actively clicked on.
optimization.desc_hr_toggle: Chooses how much internal heat recovery is credited before the heat pump is placed. It changes the source and sink profiles that both the heat pump integration and the refrigerant optimization run on, and therefore the resulting duties and COPs.

help.title: Analysis Guide
help.smart_selection_desc: Drag an area on the map to batch select streams. Red bubbles are Hot streams (waste heat), Blue bubbles are Cold streams (heat demand).
help.scenarios_desc: Save different project versions (e.g., "Night Shift" vs "Day Shift") as Scenarios to compare their energy performance side-by-side.
help.composite_curves_desc: The horizontal overlap between the Hot and Cold lines represents the heat we can recover. The remaining gaps show the external energy we still need to pay for.
help.grand_composite_curve_desc: Identifies the "Pinch Point" (the bottleneck). Pockets in the curve show where heat can be swapped internally without needing a heat pump.
help.hpi_desc: The system automatically selects the highest-efficiency heat pump for your temperatures. Higher COP values mean better electricity-to-heat conversion.
help.metrics_desc: Heating Savings: The percentage of energy saved compared to your current status quo. Aim for high recovery first!
help.tip: Tip: Use the "Report" button to generate a full PDF-ready dashboard with all your interactive charts.

metrics.min_heating_desc: The absolute minimum external heat required by the system to reach target temperatures after all possible internal heat recovery is utilized.
metrics.min_cooling_desc: The absolute minimum external cooling required by the system after all possible internal heat recovery is utilized.
metrics.pinch_temp_desc: The temperature level dividing the system into a heat sink (above pinch) and a heat source (below pinch). No heat should be transferred across the pinch.
metrics.heat_recovery_desc: The total amount of heat that can be recovered internally by matching hot and cold streams.

collection_help.title: Collection Guide
collection_help.map_ui_desc: Use the Search bar to center the map. The Lock map button disables panning so you can safely place markers without dragging the map.
collection_help.add_process_desc: Click + Add Process to create a new industrial plant group. Then click Place and click anywhere on the map to position it.
collection_help.subprocesses_desc: Expand a process to view its internals. Click + Add to create new subprocesses inside the parent process.
collection_help.connections_desc: Use next processes to draw directional arrows between boxes on the map. Use the streams table to input thermodynamic data (temperatures, mass flow, heat capacity) for pinch analysis.
collection_help.tip: Once your data is collected, switch to the Potential Analysis tab to optimize your energy recovery.
